title: Handling Objections
setup: You’re a sales rep on a discovery call with Bill, an operations manager whose team has used the same system for years.
As you start asking about his current process, Bill leans back and says:
prospectLine: Look, our current setup isn’t perfect, but it works. My team knows it, and switching sounds like a lot of pain for not much gain.
question: How will you respond?

choices.text: A lot of teams say that, but older systems like yours usually end up costing more in the long run.
choices.intent: Criticizes Bill’s current solution, which puts him on the defensive and makes him justify a choice he’s already made.

choices.text: Totally understand. What if we handled the whole migration for free so it’s no hassle?
choices.intent: Jumps to an incentive to remove friction before learning whether there’s a problem worth solving at all.

choices.text: That’s a fair concern. Switching is real work. When you say it isn’t perfect, where does it slow your team down most?
choices.intent: Validates the concern about change, then picks up on Bill’s own words to uncover pain he already admits exists.
